description.comment: The southern brook lamprey (Ichthyomyzon gagei) is a lamprey found in the Southern United States including Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, and Georgia and ranges as far north as Minnesota and Wisconsin. It is a jawless fish with a sucking mouth on one end (from Wikipedia entry). This sample of a male individual found in Wisconsin was procured by Devin Bloom of Western Michigan University to generate a somatic high-quality somatic and gametic reference genomes for the Vertebrate Genomes Project (VGP). Sequencing and genome assembly were conducted at the Vertebrate Genome Lab (VGL) at the Rockefeller University, led by Erich D. Jarvis, Giulio Formenti, and Jennifer Balacco.

assembly_info.comments: Curator note: We have submitted genome assemblies from this individual for a somatic tissue sample and a gametic tissue sample. In the literature, the karyotype for this species is 2n = 164 for somatic samples. We identified 2n = 164 chromosomes in the gametic genome assembly and 2n = 168 in the somatic genome assembly. The chromosomes in the gametic assembly were ordered and labeled by size, and the chromosomes in the somatic assembly were labeled by homology to the gametic genome. Chromosome 41 in the gametic assembly is homologous to two somatic chromosomes, chromosome 41a and chromosome 41b, the former of which aligns to one portion of gametic chromosome 41 and the latter aligning to the remainder. The Hi-C contact map gave insufficient evidence to join somatic chromosomes 41a and 41b into a single chromosome. Chromosome 83 in the somatic assembly aligns to several highly gapped, unassigned scaffolds in the gametic assembly: Scaffold_1272, Scaffold_1649, Scaffold_1645, Scaffold_1271. The Hi-C signal across these scaffolds was weak and inconclusive, so it was not possible to determine whether they should be joined into a single chromosome. Alignment between the somatic and gametic assemblies revealed several structural differences concentrated among the microchromosomes, which were generally fragmented and with weaker Hi-C signal. As a result, it is unclear whether the differences represent true biological variation or artifacts from genome assembly and/or curation. Potential inversions were identified in chromosomes 74, 75, 78, and 80, and potential translocation was identified in chromosome 82
